judgements.justification: A's AC added only 'timely' and unanimity to the scores, and B's AC followed Reviewer_16Eb; neither set the outcome from a reading of their own (A's unexplained tier is R31).
A's Reviewer_qxEj's 'might inspire new architectures' is a passing strength; no recommendation rests on an impact forecast.
No A score moved; B's Reviewer_MKzA edited to 6 but the earlier score is unknown, and B's below-threshold reviewers held.
Both committees had thin reviews (A's Reviewer_qxEj; B's Reviewer_16Eb and Reviewer_NaL7), so scrutiny was not lower on one side.
B's unique decisive concern is a utility standard (R36), not a concern about claims, method or evidence; NaL7's missing concurrent work did not reach B's AC's reasons.
Both saw the one-CNN-family limit and the shallow causal analysis; A's Reviewer_sCgD judged them non-fatal, B's reviewers and AC took them as grounds to reject.
No reviewer changed a score after reading other reviewers.
Each rating matches its review: A's 6s are mixed critiques that argue against rejection, B's 4 and 5 argue for rejection.
Confidences are 3 to 5 and no reviewer said they could not judge the paper.
B's meta-review gives two reasons that restate the lowest scorer Reviewer_16Eb's review and reply ('why this kind of representation emerges', 'only one type of architecture').
The verbal verdicts differ: B's reviewers demanded design guidance that A's never did, so the score gap is not a calibration gap.
A's AC wrote 'All reviewers recommend acceptance. Could be a spotlight' on 7/6/7/6 with no reviewer above 7 or arguing for a spotlight.
No score rose on rebuttal material.
A's three-sentence meta-review names no weakness, though Reviewer_sCgD and Reviewer_SJG2 raised the one-family, correlational-locality and normalization concerns.
B's Reviewer_16Eb (4) wrote the paper does not show why the representations emerge, but Sections 5-6 and the Figure 8 intervention do, and B's AC repeated the claim.
No damaging concession in either rebuttal.
All objections came in the reviews and were answered in the rebuttal.
The score profiles differ (means 6.5 and 5.25), so this is not one profile cut at two tier thresholds.
No committee had a clearly best-informed reviewer whose verdict the AC ignored; B's confidence-5 Reviewer_NaL7 wrote two sentences.
A's answerable concerns (normalization) got new heatmaps but A's scores did not rise, so the rebuttal lifted neither committee.
Without Reviewer_16Eb's 4, B is 6/6/5 (mean 5.67), still below A's 6.5; one score did not set the tier.
B's outlier Reviewer_16Eb replied to the rebuttal on 2021-08-31.
Neither AC discarded a detractor as unreliable.
No one raised audience breadth or venue fit.
B's AC wrote 'the reviewers all said' the study was not thorough on other CNNs; only 16Eb and fR12 said so, and fR12 and MKzA called the analysis thorough.
Three A reviewers stayed silent after the rebuttal, but that kept A's scores level and did not widen the split, so it is not a cause here.
No reviewer said they could not verify the results.
B's reviewers split two lean-accept against two below threshold at confidence 4 to 5, and the AC broke the tie toward reject by adopting Reviewer_16Eb's critique.
No evidence that the authors told the committees different things.
NaL7's concurrent-work point is about missing citations, not a wrong novelty verdict that fed a score.
A's spotlight on 7/6/7/6 with two 'marginally above' ratings has no stated grounds beyond 'timely' and unanimity.
No reviewer read the paper from a neighbouring field's premises.
Neither committee had an engaged champion above the accept level; A's 7s are the least argued reviews.
No reviewer rejected for revisions too large to accept without re-review.
B's AC cites private comments that are not in the record when breaking the two-two split toward reject.

added.name: Committees applied different standards for the contribution type
added.definition: One committee required the paper to meet a standard tied to its kind of contribution that the other committee did not apply, such as demanding that an empirical analysis paper yield practical guidance or a method, and counted its absence against the paper, while the other committee valued the contribution on its own terms.
added.justification: R05 covers a concern about claims, method or evidence that one committee missed; R06 and R24 cover weighting and venue fit. None names one committee holding the paper to a different standard of what its kind of contribution must deliver, which is B's decisive ground here.

reasoning: The spotlight-versus-reject split has two parts. B rejected because it held an analysis paper to a design-utility test that A never applied (R36) and weighted the shared one-CNN-family limit more heavily (R06). B's AC then broke a two-two split toward reject (R28) by adopting the outlying Reviewer_16Eb's framing (R10), which rested partly on a misreading (R15), overstated reviewer consensus (R25) and cited off-record private comments (R35). On A's side, the AC turned unanimous 7/6/7/6 into a spotlight with no stated grounds and no weaknesses named (R12, R14, R31). The stage 1 candidates map to existing reasons except the design-utility test, so one reason was added.
